title: the operator is a device whose bin carries the operator's verbs
intention: cairn/devices/operator/ carries a charter (the operator is Akien; this device is his seat in the system and speaks as operator) and instance 0's bin: `operator` (no words: the inbox), `show` (cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox show …), and `answer` (`cairn operator answer <id> "<words>" --spawned …`, handing off to the question door unchanged), wired into ~/.cairn/devices/operator/0/bin like every device's bin.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: No operator device exists under cairn/devices/ or ~/.cairn/devices (2026-11-05); `cairn operator` reaches bin/cmd/operator, which runs cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox; operator_inbox's main takes one verb, show (inbox | artifact <id>). Outline 8.4.4 (Q#27): answering is the operator acting, so it is `cairn operator answer`. Akien 2026-11-05 (Q#27, outline 8.4): 'if there's a script for it, run it, else get on the bus' and 'cairn help lists [all] then [operator] then [cairn] then the rest in alpha order'.
traces_to: Telos: the operator's one interface (outline 8.4). Law 1 (a shortcut is a settled route), Law 4 (script-else-bus is the dispatch, not a convention), RULE 1 (the bus is a device's public interface).
how: Write the charter through `cairn artifact write`; three bash scripts in the readlink-REPO_ROOT shape of the librarian's bin/ask, each calling its tool's public interface (python3 -m cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox; bin/cmd/question answer); wire the instance with cairn_wire_instances; red-first proof over a scratch question corpus.
falsifier: (1) cairn/devices/operator/intention+why.json exists and ~/.cairn/devices/operator/0/bin resolves to cairn/devices/operator/0/bin; (2) `cairn operator show inbox` prints the inbox through the device bin, not bin/cmd/operator; (3) `cairn operator answer <id> "<words>" --spawned none` on a scratch open question records the words verbatim exactly as `cairn question answer` does; (4) no script in the bin imports any module outside the public interfaces of operator_inbox and the question door.

decisions.text: Red-first proof cairn/devices/operator/proofs/test_the_operator_verbs_are_in_its_bin.py, check()/FAILURES/main() shape, one tooth per falsifier clause, PROVES = {'fd597e74056f': {'1': 'clause_1', '2': 'clause_2', '3': 'clause_3', '4': 'clause_4'}} (tooth names written at build). Scratch roots only — no live bus, no live store.
